target_customer: Online merchants and sellers in Singapore and Southeast Asia that need to collect bank transfer and card payments
problem: Small online sellers in Southeast Asia lacked simple, low-cost ways to accept bank transfers and card payments.
business_model: Payments gateway with per-transaction fees, later B2B payment infrastructure

founders.name: Tianwei Liu
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2016 says he worked at Amazon in the Bay Area when the idea was conceived.

founders.name: Victor Liew Jia Hao
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2016 says he worked at Quora in the Bay Area.

exit.acquirer: Fazz Financial Group (formed by PAYFAZZ and Xfers)
exit.reason: PAYFAZZ invested $30M in Xfers to form a combined group; outlets differ on whether this was a merger or an acquisition.

competitors.name: Omise
competitors.what: Bangkok-based payment gateway for Southeast Asia

competitors.name: Braintree
competitors.what: Card payments gateway owned by PayPal

technical_complexity.rationale: Connecting to local bank transfer rails and reconciling payments in several countries needed regulatory and integration work, though the core API is standard.

defensibility.rationale: Payment licences and bank integrations in Singapore and Indonesia are slow to replicate, and merchants integrate an API, but global players could expand in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Global gateways entered Southeast Asia over time, while Xfers joined PAYFAZZ in 2021 to form Fazz Financial Group.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in January 2016 reported that Xfers had processed SGD 5.5M since its API opened in October 2014, showing real merchant demand for bank transfer payments.

branding.domain_note: Used xfers.com; acquisition of the domain was not found.

identity.logo: Not described in the sources found
identity.visual_style: Not documented in the sources found
identity.voice_and_tone: Simple payments for merchants; called the PayPal of Southeast Asia by Channel News Asia per its YC description

branding.brand_signature: Called the PayPal of Southeast Asia (press framing)

rebrands.why: Part of the Fazz group branding after the Payfazz combination; exact date not found

brand_strength.rationale: A clipped respelling of transfers that is hard to spell and was later absorbed into the Fazz brand; no evidence of consumer pull.

outcome_analysis: Xfers raised a $2.5M seed in January 2016 after processing SGD 5.5M in volume, then built payments infrastructure in Singapore and Indonesia. In March 2021 PAYFAZZ invested $30M and the two formed Fazz Financial Group, with Xfers as the B2B arm and later rebranded as Fazz Business. The sources describe a combination rather than a clean sale, and the price was not disclosed, so it is a group formation that the YC directory labels an acquisition.
notes: xfers.com returned 403 when fetched; not a dead site. Competitors come from the January 2016 TechCrunch seed article, close to the batch but a few months after it. A Fazz Series C ($100M led by Tiger Global, 2022) belongs to the Fazz group and is not recorded as an Xfers round. DailySocial calls the 2021 deal an acquisition; Fintech News says investment forming a group. Founder education not found. No Series A or B for Xfers found.
